..
Issued at 155 AM CDT Wed Oct 28 2026

As of 1am temperatures are in the upper 30s to the upper 40s with 
winds mainly out of the southeast between 5-10mph. Satellite 
imagery continues to indicate low stratus surging northward east of 
the James River with KATY reporting a cloud deck of 600ft. Otherwise 
patchy to areas of fog continue to develop between the Missouri and 
James River with webcams indicating some of that being dense in 
areas. Have not issued a Fog Headline just yet as winds continue to 
keep things above criteria for now but will continue to monitor 
webcams and obs through the morning.

Our next shortwave continues to move in from the west and by 12Z, 
the axis of this wave will be over WY through CO with the region on 
the PVA side of it in southwest flow. At the surface the center of 
the low is forecast to be over west central SD with a weak trough 
connecting to a secondary low over northwestern KS. This is all 
within a large area of low pressure extending from a system in 
central Canada. On the northern side of the quasi stationary/warm 
front to start (mainly west to east across the center half of the 
state), CAMs do indicate a band(s)of elevated rain showers 
developing over WY/western SD and tracking northeast across portions 
of north central and northeastern SD into ND early this morning and 
more on the northern/northeast side of the low (as it tracks 
northeast) through the midday. By 18Z the center of the low will be 
near ND/SD/MN border with its fropa extending through eastern SD. 
With additional forcing from its shortwave and an 85-100kt jet 
aloft, dewpoints warming into the lower to mid 50s, and daytime 
heating, additional showers and even thunderstorms will develop 
ahead/along the front James Valley and eastward ~late morning/midday 
through the afternoon.

The resulting pops per NBM is 50-85% chance east of the James River 
with the highest pops Coteau and eastward. Coteau and eastward is 
really where HRRR/REFS does indicate spotty convective development 
(right along the front) over this area around ~17-18Z with these 
cells quickly moving into MN by ~22-23Z. NAMNest and RAP are a bit 
slower on the exit and a bit more westward extent of convection. NBM 
does a good job overall with coverage and timing due to a bit of a 
difference between the CAMS. Not too much SFC CAPE to work with 
(MUCAPE under 1000j/kg) but we do have the shear of 40-50kts and 
steep lapse rates of 6-7C/km Coteau and eastward between ~19-22Z 
this afternoon. So low cape high shear scenario. So for a few hours 
there will be enough energy for weak thunderstorms. Further east 
(far eastern SD/MN) if we can get enough vertical development into 
the cooler air aloft there could be the threat for an isolated cell 
or two to become severe(60 mph gusts/quarter hail), however, any 
more organized convection is forecast to remain further east into MN 
with better moisture/forcing. Very far portions of east central SD 
is within the 5% chance of severe weather for hail, per CSU ML 
guidance, which does back this up. WIth this threat, the SPC has 
expanded the Marginal Risk westward east of Interstate 29 through 
west central MN. Main threats include 1" diameter hail and 60 mph 
wind gusts. The last of the precip is forecast to exit by 00Z. 

As the front track across the CWA winds will shift to the 
west/northwest behind it as drier air moves in aloft and high 
pressure filters in from the west/northwest. As winds become light 
tonight and ongoing moisture at the surface from the recent rains, 
plus radiational cooling, soundings once again do indicate this low 
level saturation below a strong inversion from the surface up to 
950mb or so. REFS/HREF do indicate the formation of "low clouds" 
over the region overnight so lower confidence on if this is just low 
stratus forming or in fact fog. Probably of visibility at a 1/4th 
mile or less is 45-65% mainly across the James Valley and the Coteau 
per both HREF/REFS and once again NBM keeping low chances. So will 
watch the potential for this. Otherwise, high pressure keeps the 
area dry Thursday and Friday before another shortwave/low brings in 
additional chances of rain Friday night through Saturday night and 
again early next week.
